title: Biotech news from around the world - Nature Biotechnology
gist: Nature Biotechnology's news roundup reports that CRISPR-Cas9 editing of myostatin raised rainbow trout body weight by 56%, and that Seoul-based DuChemBio will build Korea's first dedicated radiopharmaceutical plant under a $25.5 million contract, opening in 2029.

insights.claim: Injecting two guide RNAs targeting the first exon of the myostatin gene mstnb1 into fertilized rainbow trout eggs increased the fish's body weight by 56%, per Ataturk University scientists.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A 56% weight gain from one edit suggests gene-edited aquaculture could cut production cycles; regulatory approval of edited fish is the gating item to monitor.
insights.quote: the team was able to increase the trouts’ body weight by 56%

insights.claim: The authors suggest CRISPR-Cas9 could shorten production time and improve production efficiency in aquaculture.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Efficiency gains in fish farming would flow to producers and feed suppliers if edited stock is commercialised.
insights.quote: The results suggest that CRISPR–Cas9 could help shorten production time and improve production efficiency in aquaculture.

insights.claim: DuChemBio agreed a $25.5 million contract with North Jeolla Province and the city of Jeongeup to build Korea's first plant dedicated to radiopharmaceuticals.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Public-private funding for radioisotope capacity points to growing regional supply-chain investment in radiopharmaceuticals.
insights.quote: Seoul-based pharma DuChemBio will build Korea’s first plant dedicated to radiopharmaceuticals

insights.claim: The DuChemBio facility will combine radioisotope production, drug manufacturing and export, with construction starting in mid-2027 and opening targeted for 2029.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A 2029 opening means no near-term supply impact; watch for construction start in mid-2027.
insights.quote: The facility will combine radioisotope production, drug manufacturing and export.
